leftEvidence.title: Jesus dies, his side is pierced, and the narrator insists on eyewitness testimony

points.label: Visible body
points.left: Thirst, death, unbroken legs, a pierced side, blood, and water belong to the narrated body.
points.right: The Lamb stands as though slain, with horns and eyes, at the center of the throne scene.

points.label: Witness and speech
points.left: The narrator confirms seeing and cites Scripture.
points.right: Elders and living creatures sing about slaughter, blood, peoples, and kingdom.

payload.posture: The sources independently preserve the relationship named by a pierced body witnessed / a lamb standing as slain.

rightEvidence.title: A Lamb stands as slain, takes the scroll, and is praised for purchasing people by blood

payload.tension: The later vision reuses slaughter and blood imagery without becoming a second narration of Golgotha.
payload.title: A pierced body witnessed / a Lamb standing as slain
